criterion_notes.c1: Examines municipal drinking water supply (acueducto) and sewerage (alcantarillado) service coverage of residential properties across urban, rural, and total municipal areas in Colombia (2008-2019).
criterion_notes.c2: Passes the plain wording of Criterion 2 but fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading. Under the plain wording, the study examines institutional, administrative, and governance factors—specifically the fiscal (SGP earmarked intergovernmental transfers, municipal property/total tax collection, royalties), political (mayoral electoral competition and voter turnout), and administrative (Municipal Performance Measurement [MDM] management index) dimensions of Colombian decentralization. Under the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism scope, however, it fails Criterion 2 (exclude as E03, Wrong exposure) because these independent variables are macro-decentralization, public-finance, electoral, and aggregate municipal management capacity indicators (alongside municipal size and geography), rather than a rule-type legal, regulatory, or administrative mechanism directly governing household or community service access (eligibility screening, administrative burden, documentation or tenure requirements, tariff or cost-recovery rules, discretion or accommodation, enforcement, or utility ownership or regulatory structure directly governing service access).
criterion_notes.c3: Quantitative empirical panel study estimating Hausman-Taylor panel regressions across Colombian municipalities over three four-year mayoral terms (2008-2011, 2012-2015, 2016-2019) using official SSPD, CEDE, DNP, CGR, and RNEC datasets.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports municipal residential coverage rates (%) for conventional drinking water supply (acueducto) and sewerage (alcantarillado) across total, urban, and rural areas from SSPD's Reporte de Estratificación y Cobertura (REC).
criterion_notes.c5: Clearly identifies the unit of analysis and sample (Colombian municipalities; up to 1,063 descriptively and N = 893 municipalities / 2,188 observations for water and N = 877 / 2,179 for sewerage in panel regressions), fiscal/political/administrative/geographic exposures, service coverage outcomes, and Hausman-Taylor panel econometric design.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish with an English title and abstract; direct translation of the Spanish full text is feasible per Inclusion Criterion 10 (to be logged in extraction_note if included).

evidence_quotes.quote: This paper examines the effects of fiscal, political, and administrative dimensions of Colombian decentralization on the performance of municipal governments in providing water supply and sewerage services between 2008 and 2019.

raw_response.exposure: Fiscal, political, and administrative dimensions of municipal decentralization and geographic/size factors: per-capita SGP water transfers, municipal property and total tax revenues, and royalties; mayoral electoral competition (effective number of parties, top-two vote share) and voter turnout; Municipal Performance Measurement (MDM) management score; and municipal size category, altitude, natural region, and functional urban area status
raw_response.outcome: Municipal residential coverage rates (%) of conventional drinking water supply (acueducto) and sewerage (alcantarillado) services across total, urban, and rural areas
raw_response.population_and_sample: Colombian municipalities (unit of analysis: municipality), covering up to 1,063 municipalities descriptively and 893 municipalities (2,188 municipality-period observations) for drinking water and 877 municipalities (2,179 observations) for sewerage across three four-year mayoral terms (2008-2011, 2012-2015, 2016-2019), stratified into small (categories 4-6) and medium/large (special and categories 1-3) municipalities
raw_response.rationale: This Spanish-language econometric panel study (with English abstract) examines municipal drinking water and sewerage residential coverage in Colombia (2008-2019), satisfying c1, c3, c4, c5, and c6 (translation feasible per Criterion 10). Under the plain wording of Criterion 2, it would be included because it evaluates fiscal, political, and administrative decentralization factors. Under the active 2026-10-13 narrow rule-type reading of Criterion 2, however, it is excluded as E03 (Wrong exposure): its empirical exposures are macro-fiscal public-finance flows (intergovernmental transfers, local taxes, royalties), electoral competition/turnout, an aggregate municipal management index (MDM), and geography/municipal size, rather than a rule-type legal, regulatory, or administrative mechanism directly governing household or community service access (such as eligibility screening, administrative burden, tenure/documentation rules, tariff/cost-recovery rules, discretion, enforcement, or utility ownership/regulatory structure).
raw_response.study_design: Observational longitudinal panel data study (three four-year mayoral-term periods, 2008-2019) using Hausman-Taylor panel regressions
